subproblem.title: A.e. strong measurability of sqrt det(p L* L p + I − p) for a.e. strongly measurable operator fields p, L
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, E := ℝ^P (Euclid P), μ a measure on E, and p, L : E → End(E) := (E →L[ℝ] E) (operator-norm topology) both μ-a.e. strongly measurable. Then x ↦ sqrt(det(p(x) ∘ (L(x)* ∘ L(x)) ∘ p(x) + (I − p(x)))) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, where L(x)* is the adjoint of L(x), I is the identity of E and det is the determinant of an endomorphism of E.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (p L : Euclid P → (Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P)), AEStronglyMeasurable p μ → AEStronglyMeasurable L μ → AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => Real.sqrt ((p x ∘L ((L x).adjoint ∘L L x) ∘L p x + (ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Euclid P) - p x)).det)) μ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3–4 of the parent proof (continuity of Φ(p, A) = det(p ∘ A* ∘ A ∘ p + (I − p)) on End(E) × End(E), followed by composition with the a.e. strongly measurable pair (p, L)); this makes precise Simon's remark that J^M_f is H^n-measurable (Ch. 3, the remark 'Thus J^M_f is H^n-measurable' in the proof of 2.4, book/chapter-03.txt line 385; formula 2.3 is at line 365). Details are filled in below.

Notation. E := Euclid P; End(E) := E →L[ℝ] E with its operator-norm topology; I := ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ E; B* := B.adjoint for B ∈ End(E); det := ContinuousLinearMap.det (= LinearMap.det of the underlying linear map).

1. Reduction to a continuous function of the pair. Define Φ : End(E) × End(E) → ℝ by
 Φ(q, B) := sqrt(det(q ∘ ((B* ∘ B) ∘ q) + (I − q))).
 For every x ∈ E, the function in the statement takes the value Φ(p x, L x): the two expressions coincide verbatim after substituting q := p x and B := L x (in Lean, `p x ∘L ((L x).adjoint ∘L L x) ∘L p x` parses as `p x ∘L (((L x).adjoint ∘L L x) ∘L p x)` because ∘L is right-associative, which is the same shape).

2. Φ is continuous. (a) The projections (q, B) ↦ q and (q, B) ↦ B are continuous (continuous_fst, continuous_snd). (b) B ↦ B* is continuous on End(E): ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint is a linear isometric equivalence End(E) ≃ End(E) (over ℝ the conjugation is trivial), hence continuous; so (q, B) ↦ B* is continuous. (c) Composition of continuous linear maps is jointly continuous, (S, R) ↦ S ∘ R being a bounded bilinear map (Continuous.clm_comp); hence (q, B) ↦ B* ∘ B, then (q, B) ↦ (B* ∘ B) ∘ q, then (q, B) ↦ q ∘ ((B* ∘ B) ∘ q) are continuous. (d) (q, B) ↦ I − q is continuous (constant minus a continuous map), and a sum of continuous maps is continuous (Continuous.sub, Continuous.add); so (q, B) ↦ q ∘ ((B* ∘ B) ∘ q) + (I − q) is continuous. (e) det : End(E) → ℝ is continuous because E is finite-dimensional (ContinuousLinearMap.continuous_det). (f) Real.sqrt is continuous (Real.continuous_sqrt). Composing (a)–(f), Φ is continuous.

3. The pair is a.e. strongly measurable. Since p and L are μ-a.e. strongly measurable, so is x ↦ (p x, L x) : E → End(E) × End(E) (AEStronglyMeasurable.prodMk).

4. Conclusion. The composition of a continuous map with a μ-a.e. strongly measurable map is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable). Hence x ↦ Φ(p x, L x) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, and by step 1 this is exactly the function x ↦ sqrt(det(p x ∘ ((L x)* ∘ L x) ∘ p x + (I − p x))) of the statement. ∎

Formalization note (complete script checked with `lake env lean` in this repository's pinned environment, Lean v4.35.0-rc3, Mathlib 25730c7c, inside `namespace GMT.Ch07` / `namespace Submission` with the frozen contract's `open`s; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). Important: form the composite with `have h := …` and close with `exact h`; writing `exact hΦ.comp_aestronglyMeasurable (hp.prodMk hL)` directly against the goal made elaboration hit the 200000-heartbeat limit (deterministic timeout at whnf) in testing.
  intro P μ p L hp hL
  have hadj : Continuous fun q : (Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P) × (Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P) => (q.2).adjoint :=
    (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (𝕜 := ℝ) (E := Euclid P) (F := Euclid P)).continuous.comp continuous_snd
  have hΦ : Continuous fun q : (Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P) × (Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P) =>
      Real.sqrt ((q.1 ∘L ((q.2).adjoint ∘L q.2) ∘L q.1 + (ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Euclid P) - q.1)).det) := by
    refine Real.continuous_sqrt.comp (ContinuousLinearMap.continuous_det.comp ?_)
    refine Continuous.add ?_ (continuous_const.sub continuous_fst)
    exact continuous_fst.clm_comp ((hadj.clm_comp continuous_snd).clm_comp continuous_fst)
  have h := hΦ.comp_aestronglyMeasurable (hp.prodMk hL)
  exact h
proof_key_steps: The given function is x ↦ Φ(p x, L x) with Φ(q, B) := sqrt(det(q∘((B*∘B)∘q) + (I − q))) on End(E) × End(E).
Φ is continuous: projections, the adjoint (a linear isometric equivalence), jointly continuous composition (clm_comp), + and −, det (continuous in finite dimension) and Real.sqrt are continuous.
x ↦ (p x, L x) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.prodMk).
Continuous ∘ a.e. strongly measurable is a.e. strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable).
